Need, adoption and value

AI authorisations & venture investment

Authorisations indicate product availability; venture investment supports development and expansion. Neither directly measures paid adoption. Periods and coverage must match before drawing comparisons; the two series are shown separately to avoid an implied correlation.

Modality and clinical application show where product supply is concentrated and where gaps may remain. Authorisation shares are not usage or revenue shares. Each authorisation has one category in each breakdown; unclassified entries remain visible.

Data coverage & interpretation
  • Reported values come from named sources; estimates retain their methodology and scope.
  • Clinical pressure creates a potential need for AI, while budgets and implementation capacity determine purchasing.
  • FDA authorisations measure regulatory activity, not hospital adoption or the number of unique commercial products.
  • Consumer price indices are cost-pressure proxies; they do not directly measure hospital input costs.
  • Equity benchmarks reflect wider healthcare sentiment rather than the imaging AI market itself.
